chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Durost ibn Abi Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is prejudicial or is been prejudicial to, so the rein of Emān has been loosened from his neck'.

key_terms.تَعَصَّبَ: To be prejudicial or show bias/tribalism

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to have the rein of faith loosened from one's neck in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, 'ta'assub' is often interpreted broadly to include tribalism, nationalism, and partisan loyalty that supersedes divine truth, as discussed by commentators like Al-Majlisi in *Bihar al-Anwar*. This hadith serves as a foundational critique of *asabiyyah* (group solidarity), warning that such bias effectively removes the 'yoke' or bond of faith, rendering one's religious commitment superficial. It underscores the necessity of purifying the heart from all forms of exclusive allegiance to ensure genuine adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings.
